ground_truth_witness: n = 2, V = {0,1}, M = M' = {{0,1}}. Both are perfect matchings of V. G = (V, M u M') has edge set {{0,1}} and its single connected component has 2 vertices, 1 edge, degrees (1,1). Claim says every component is an isolated vertex or a cycle; this component is NOT an isolated vertex (that requires 1 vertex and 0 edges; here 2 vertices, 1 edge) and NOT a cycle (a simple-graph cycle requires >= 3 vertices with #edges = #vertices; here #vertices = 2 < 3). The same failure occurs whenever M and M' merely SHARE one edge, e.g. n = 4 with M = M' = {{0,1},{2,3}} (both components are single edges), or M = {{0,1},{2,3}}, M' = {{0,1},{2,3}}. More generally the exhaustive run found 502,567 single-edge components across the space and ZERO isolated-vertex components.
ground_truth_flaw: In the graph G on vertex set V with edge set M ∪ M' (M, M' perfect matchings), every connected component is either an isolated vertex or a cycle.
